Before libvirt modifies the MAC address and vlan tag for an SRIOV VF
for use by a virtual machine (either using vfio device assignment or
macvtap passthru mode)
column2: it saves the current MAC address and vlan tag

column1: so that it can reset them to their original value when the guest is
done.  Libvirt can't leave the VF MAC set to the value used by the
now-defunct guest since it may be started again later using a
different VF
column2: but it certainly shouldn't just pick any random value

column1: either. So it saves the state of everything prior to using the VF
resets it to that.
The igb driver initializes the MAC addresses of all VFs to

column2: and reports that when asked (via an RTM_GETLINK

column1: netlink message
column2: also visible in the list of VFs in the output of ""ip

column1: link show""). But when libvirt attempts to restore the MAC address back
to 00:00:00:00:00:00 (using an RTM_SETLINK netlink message) the kernel
responds with ""Invalid argument"".
Forbidding a reset back to the original value leaves the VF MAC at the
value set for the now-defunct virtual machine. Especially on a system
with NetworkManager enabled
NetworkManager forces all interfacess to be IFF_UP all the time - if
the same virtual machine is restarted using a different VF (or even on
a different host)
column2: there will be multiple interfaces watching for

column1: traffic with the same MAC address.
To allow libvirt to revert to the original state
remove the administrative set MAC on a VF
operation again
column2: and to reset/overwrite the VF MAC via VF netdev.

column1: This patch implements the outlined scenario by allowing to set the
VF MAC to 00:00:00:00:00:00 via RTM_SETLINK on the PF.
igb_ndo_set_vf_mac resets the IGB_VF_FLAG_PF_SET_MAC flag to 0
so it's possible to reset the VF MAC back to the original value via
the VF netdev.
Note: Recent patches to libvirt allow for a workaround if the NIC
isn't capable of resetting the administrative MAC back to all 0
in theory the NIC should allow resetting the MAC in the first place.
